Nifurpirinol is implicated in targeting the G(I)/G(S)/G(O) subunit gamma-2, which is a component of G-protein coupled receptors. This subunit is subsequently targeted by trans-urocanic acid, a compound that likely modulates the activity of the G-protein signaling pathway. The final step in this chain involves SK-VLB, indicating that Nifurpirinol may influence SK-VLB through the activation or inhibition of the G(I)/G(S)/G(O) subunit gamma-2. The presence of a final score of 0.5112 suggests some level of confidence in this relationship, though further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the direct interaction between Nifurpirinol and SK-VLB. The evidence highlights a possible mechanism by which Nifurpirinol could exert its effects on SK-VLB, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be elucidated.
